title: Elementary Notes on Sets (generated fixture)
fixture: tests/e2e/make_pdf.py writes the booklet; tests/e2e/make_notes_repos.py writes notes-a and notes-b and plants the defects below with scripts/score/mutate.py.
what_this_is: The ground truth for the two synthetic companions: eight planted defects, three decoys that must not be reported, and every remaining locus marked clean. `cf score` joins findings to it on (source_id, repo, item, kind), which is run-independent, so the same key scores a model fleet and the model-free detector alike.
what_this_is_not: A measurement of any real companion. The defects here were planted by a script into a fixture; a score over it measures a configuration against this fixture and nothing else (references/method.md S10).
how_to_reproduce: bash tests/e2e/synthetic.sh            # builds the workspace and scores it
cf score --run detect-notes-a-cheap --run detect-notes-b-cheap --run anchor-check-anonymous-elementary-sets --answer-key tests/e2e/answer-key.json

mechanical.what: `cf detect-proxies` for both companions plus the PAGE_ANCHOR rows `cf pair` writes -- no model anywhere.
mechanical.note: it finds every defect of the three kinds it can see and none of the four it cannot, which is the point: the free detector's recall ceiling is the mechanical half of the key.

entries.why: the booklet defines the Jordan inner measure as a supremum of elementary measures; this hands back the library's own jordanContent, so every later statement about it holds by construction.
the booklet asks only that a finite union of boxes is elementary; this adds a positivity hypothesis it never states, so the exercise is proved about less than it asks.
the booklet defines the Jordan outer measure as an infimum of elementary measures; this hands back the library's own jordanContent.
the booklet states Definition 1.4.1 (Lebesgue outer measure) and notes-b tags no declaration to it: the concept is neither defined nor used under the book's name.
translation invariance is stated for every shift k; this pins k to 1, so the exercise is proved for one translation instead of all of them.
the booklet asks for a bounded set that is NOT Jordan measurable; the negation is dropped and what is left holds by rfl.
the booklet prints Exercise 1.4.4 on page 10; the docstring anchors it at page 4, so a worker sent to the anchor reads the wrong page.
the booklet's Lemma 1.4.2 is countable SUBadditivity; the inequality is stated the other way round, which is a different (and false) claim.
notes-a carries a second, equivalent spelling (boxAlt) of the same definition. A naming convention, not a difference of content.
